liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Lost Sailor** (2 reviews, 1 other source): Reviewer says this was the first performance of Lost Sailor; First played this night after a long drought of new songs; Bob struggles to stay on the notes [8][17][19]
- **Playin' In The Band** (3 reviews): Runs about twenty minutes and is interesting; the mp3 has a one-second glitch around 11:40; Reviewer says this version soars far out before the drums; recommends hearing Shakedown Street into Playin' at least [12][15][16]
- **Shakedown Street** (2 reviews): Brent uses a funky old-school synth effect here, as on other tunes around this period; Brent's playing pushes Jerry to great guitar work, and the band sounds like they are enjoying themselves [21][22]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Listed as the opener, but it is absent from this copy of the show [16]
- **Althea** (1 review): Reviewer says this was the first performance of Althea [17]
- **Passenger** (1 review): Reviewer calls the second-set Passenger a blazing standout that left a lasting impression [14]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Garcia sounds lost in his solo, repeating one lick; Weir starts Sugar Magnolia before Jerry is ready [12]

## Setlist highlights

- **Crowd / Happy Birthday Jerry**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1979-08-04.148940.fob.sony.ecm270.severson.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): audience recording; 22 songs; 192 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]. Said about its sound: Tape flips in Deal and Drums have no patch source available [1]
- **gd1979-08-04.175376.akg.d224e.cassettemaster.hohlwein.menke.miller.flac2496**: source not stated; 21 songs; 170 min [6]
- **gd1979-08-04.sbd.munder.tetzeli.fix-9578.34259.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 160 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [7]. Said about its sound: The opener is missing from this soundboard, per Deadlists; Dropouts and cuts: Minglewood at 4:52, five seconds missing in Samson, Playin' dropout at 11:30, Drums at 10:06 [7]
- **gd1979-08-04.144160.sbd.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644**: soundboard; 22 songs; 162 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [8]
- **gd79-08-04.sbd.munder.9578.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 160 min; rated 3.68/5 by 28 [9]. Said about its sound: Brent is more prominent in the mix than usual, and may be worth checking on set one tunes too; Playing is tight but the mix is off; vocals are nearly lost on the first-set tracks; Mix is odd: vocals sit low and Bobby's guitar is slightly down, while Brent and Jerry are upfront; drums fine [12][13][14][16]

## Around the show

- Reviewer was there and recalls a wild street-fair atmosphere outside before the show [19]
- Jerry played "Tiger" live for the first time at this show [1]
- Jerry played "Tiger" live for the first time at this show [6]
- Bob sings better the next night, which the reviewer thinks is the better show overall [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1979-08-04.148940.fob.sony.ecm270.severson.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Sony ECM-270 mics (mounted on pole, right center, held shoulder high, 40' from stage)> Sony TC-158SD (Maxell… [1]
- **gd1979-08-04.175376.akg.d224e.cassettemaster.hohlwein.menke.miller.flac2496**: taped by Reinhart Hohlwein; transferred by Bob Menke; Charlie Miller; source: AKG D224E > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5) [6]. Also: Cassette master recorded with AKG D224E mics; Bob Menke's involvement made the release possible; Joe B. Jones supplied pitch correction settings [6]
- **gd1979-08-04.sbd.munder.tetzeli.fix-9578.34259.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Willy Munder and Bill Tetzeli; source: SBD>MC>C>DAT>CDR [7]. Also: Willy retracked and verified with CD Wave and Shntool; Bill made the transition between CDs 2 and 3 seamless [7]
- **gd1979-08-04.144160.sbd.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Tim Dalton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Master Soundboard Cassettes > Cassette > PCM > Dat (16-bit/44.1k) [8]. Also: Severson's Sony ECM 270 source supplies the final 29 seconds, plus a 2:53 patch in Playin' In The Band [8]
- **gd79-08-04.sbd.munder.9578.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [9]
